nodes.label: ADR 002 — Publishing requires an explicit --apply
nodes.rationale: Accepted. Every command that writes to a live GoodData org is a read-only rehearsal by default and writes only with --apply. The rehearsal runs the whole pipeline (preflight, datasource resolution, placeholder substitution, assert_fully_resolved, backup, diff) and stops at the three write calls; a backup of the target's current layout is taken immediately before the PUT, and --no-backup is refused without --apply. WHY: put_declarative_workspace has REPLACE semantics — it overwrites a workspace's entire content in one call; targets are real (petertomko.demo.cloud, the local-inference host) and API tokens are often scoped more broadly than the workspace; a mistyped profile with a write-by-default CLI silently destroys a layout that exists nowhere else. Mirrors terraform plan/apply, which the user already works in. Rejected: write-by-default + --dry-run (the dangerous path is the accidental one; rated High/High in the spec risk table), interactive confirmation (breaks CI and agents, gets muscle-memoried away), automatic backup only (recovery, not prevention; restoring 2.9 MB into a live org is itself risky). Trade-offs: every real publish is two commands; docs and CI must carry --apply; a test must pin the default. Rehearsal still reads from the host, so it is not offline and still needs credentials. Revisit only by adding a per-profile require_apply:false opt-out in config/targets.yaml for throwaway orgs, never by flipping the global default.
